key_insight: A multi-aspect, multi-agent framework effectively combines specialized reasoning about text, visual cues, and contextual signals to identify depressive symptoms in memes, supported by the new RESTOREx resource for training and evaluation.
problem_solved: Detecting depressive symptoms conveyed via multimodal memes — which mix images, overlaid text, sarcasm, and cultural context — where single-stream models often miss subtle, multi-aspect signals.
method: Multi-aspect decomposition: break meme interpretation into complementary aspects (e.g., literal text, visual sentiment, humor/sarcasm, contextual cues).
Multi-agent collaboration: deploy specialized agents (or modules) to analyze each aspect and aggregate their judgments via a coordination/ensemble mechanism.
Benchmarking on RESTOREx: curate and use a multimodal dataset/resource for supervised training and evaluation, with large language models or multimodal encoders as reasoners.
impact: Provides a practical architecture and dataset for more accurate, interpretable multimodal mental-health screening in social media content, enabling AI/ML teams to build safer, more sensitive monitoring tools and to study cross-aspect reasoning in multimodal models.

paper_title: MAMA-Memeia! Multi-Aspect Multi-Agent Collaboration for Depressive Symptoms Identification in Memes
paper_authors: Siddhant Agarwal, Adya Dhuler, Polly Ruhnke, Melvin Speisman, Md Shad Akhtar
